method.attribution: All references retrieved from PubMed; DOIs as returned by the PubMed tool.
method.fallback_tools_needed: none - the primary PubMed MCP tools responded (one call was rate-limited and retried); Consensus and the plugin PubMed server were not needed
method.evidence_grading: a=controlled human study > b=pharmacovigilance or cohort > c=review or clinical pharmacology > d=human genetic only; case reports marked weak

verdict_rule.keep as human: human pharmacological evidence for the claimed target, direction and symptom
verdict_rule.keep but relabel to <symptom>: human evidence exists for that target and direction but names a different symptom
verdict_rule.keep as rodent only: no human evidence for the symptom, but the mechanism has indirect human support (inverse-direction pharmacology, obligatory subunit, or human genetics) worth retaining as a rodent-derived hypothesis
verdict_rule.drop: no human pharmacological evidence, and either no human drug is selective enough to test the claim or a selective human drug exists and controlled data show the symptom does not occur

drugs: regadenoson (selective A2A agonist, IV, short-acting)
istradefylline (A2A ANTAGONIST - opposite direction)
other_targets_they_hit: regadenoson exposure is brief and essentially peripheral/coronary; no CNS psychomotor endpoint has been measured

references.quote: REG appears to be safe and well tolerated without significant cardiovascular adverse events.
Istradefylline is a selective adenosine A2A receptor antagonist for the treatment of patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) experiencing OFF episodes while on levodopa/decarboxylase inhibitor.
OFF hours/day were reduced at Week 12 at istradefylline dosages of 20 mg/day ... Dyskinesia was the most frequent adverse event (placebo, 9.6%; 20 mg/day, 16.1%; 40 mg/day, 17.7%).

claims.note: No human A2A agonist study has measured psychomotor slowing; regadenoson trials report only cardiovascular tolerability. The only direction-relevant human data are inverse: the selective A2A antagonist istradefylline reduces OFF time and increases dyskinesia in Parkinson's disease, which is consistent with A2A activation being motor-suppressive but is not evidence that activation produces the symptom in people.

drugs: piclidenoson (CF101), selective oral A3 adenosine receptor agonist
other_targets_they_hit: none of consequence - piclidenoson is A3-selective

references.quote: We investigated the efficacy/safety of piclidenoson (CF101), an orally bioavailable A3AR agonist that inhibits IL-17 and IL-23 production in keratinocytes, in moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis.
The safety/tolerability profile of piclidenoson was excellent and superior to apremilast.

claims.note: A selective human A3 agonist has been taken to phase 3 in psoriasis with an explicitly excellent tolerability profile and no psychomotor or CNS depressant signal. Selective human pharmacology exists and does not reproduce the claim.

drugs: none; alpha-1 agonists in human use (phenylephrine, midodrine) are peripherally acting pressors with no alpha-1B subtype selectivity
claims.note: No alpha-1B-subtype-selective agonist exists for human use, and the available alpha-1 agonists are vasopressors without central psychomotor endpoints. No reference is cited because no human study of alpha-1B activation and psychomotor retardation was found.

drugs: none; every CACNA1C-directed human drug (dihydropyridines, verapamil, diltiazem) is a BLOCKER, i.e. the opposite direction
claims.note: There is no Cav1.2 activator in human use, so the activation direction cannot be tested pharmacologically in people. CACNA1C gain-of-function (Timothy syndrome) produces long QT, syndactyly and neurodevelopmental/autistic features rather than psychomotor retardation; no verifiable human phenotype paper making the psychomotor-retardation claim was found, so no genetic reference is credited.

drugs: sincalide/CCK-8 (gallbladder imaging; hits CCKAR and CCKBR)
CCK-4 is a CCKBR/CCK2 agonist, not CCKAR
other_targets_they_hit: CCKBR (CCK2) - the receptor responsible for the only well-characterised human CCK challenge effect

references.quote: Cholecystokinin-tetrapeptide (CCK-4)-induced panic attacks are reportedly attenuated by effective treatment with antipanic antidepressants in patients with panic disorder, but in healthy volunteers such effects are not well studied.

claims.note: The human CCK challenge literature uses CCK-4, a CCK2/CCKBR agonist, and the symptom it produces is panic, not psychomotor retardation. No human CCKAR-selective agonist has been shown to slow psychomotor function.

drugs: xanomeline-trospium (KarXT), M1/M4-preferring muscarinic agonist
other_targets_they_hit: CHRM4 (xanomeline is a dual M1/M4-preferring agonist)

references.quote: Xanomeline is a dual Mand M-preferring muscarinic receptor agonist that does not block Ddopamine receptors

Treatment-emergent adverse event rates of extrapyramidal motor symptoms (KarXT, zero [0%] vs placebo, zero [0%]), akathisia (one [1%] vs one [1%]), weight gain (zero [0%] vs one [1%]), and somnolence (six [5%] vs five [4%]) were similar between the KarXT and placebo groups

claims.note: The one phase 3 human trial of an M1-preferring agonist found somnolence no different from placebo (5% vs 4%) and zero extrapyramidal motor adverse events; adverse effects were gastrointestinal and autonomic. This is controlled human evidence against the claim, and xanomeline cannot separate M1 from M4 in any case.

drugs: delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol / dronabinol (CB1 partial agonist)
other_targets_they_hit: CNR2 (CB2) - THC is a CB1/CB2 partial agonist; smoked cannabis additionally contains cannabidiol and other constituents
claims.symptom_the_human_data_support: psychomotor impairment (slowed/degraded psychomotor and cognitive performance), not the depressive sign of psychomotor retardation

references.quote: Task performance was impaired after THC administration, reflected in both an increase in false alarms and a reduction in detected targets.
THC induced more robust cognitive impairment compared with MDMA, and co-administration did not exacerbate single drug effects on cognitive function.
This study indicates that dronabinol did not enhance the analgesic effects of oxycodone and increased abuse- and impairment-related subjective effects.

claims.verdict: keep but relabel to psychomotor impairment
claims.note: Multiple randomised placebo-controlled crossover studies in healthy volunteers show THC degrades psychomotor and sustained-attention performance. This is genuine human drug-induced psychomotor slowing and CB1 agonism is the principal action, but the measured construct is performance impairment rather than the observable motor-and-speech slowing meant by psychomotor retardation.

drugs: zolpidem and zaleplon (alpha1-preferring GABA-A benzodiazepine-site agonists)
other_targets_they_hit: alpha2, alpha3 and alpha5 GABA-A subunits are bound at higher doses; selectivity is preference, not absolute
claims.symptom_the_human_data_support: sedation with psychomotor impairment

references.quote: Zaleplon is a novel pyrazolopyrimidine hypnotic agent that acts as a selective agonist to the brain omega(1) receptor situated on the alpha(1) subunit of the GABA(A) receptor complex.

consistent detrimental residual effects on various aspects of psychomotor and cognitive functions were observed with the therapeutic doses of the various commonly prescribed hypnotic agents used as comparators, e.g. zolpidem 10 mg up to 5 h after dose administration
Although both triazolam and zolpidem increased overall reaction time in the negative priming task, only triazolam increased the magnitude of negative priming relative to placebo.

claims.verdict: keep but relabel to sedation with psychomotor impairment
claims.note: This is the only GABA-A subunit with a genuinely subunit-preferring human drug. Controlled studies and a clinical pharmacology review document dose-dependent psychomotor and driving impairment and increased reaction time with zolpidem/zaleplon. The human construct is sedation-linked psychomotor impairment, so the claim should be relabelled rather than kept as psychomotor retardation.

drugs: TPA023, an alpha2/alpha3-selective GABA-A partial agonist tested in humans
other_targets_they_hit: GABRA3 - TPA023 cannot separate alpha2 from alpha3

references.quote: binds with equivalent high (subnanomolar) affinity to the benzodiazepine binding site of recombinant human GABA(A) receptors containing an alpha1, alpha2, alpha3, or alpha5 subunit but has partial agonist efficacy at the alpha2 and alpha3 subtypes and essentially antagonist efficacy at the alpha1 and alpha5 subtypes

TPA023 was clearly differentiated from the nonselective agonist lorazepam in terms of saccadic eye movement and unlike lorazepam, it did not impair either postural stability, as judged by body sway, or cognition.

claims.note: An alpha2/alpha3-selective positive modulator was taken into human studies and explicitly did NOT impair body sway or cognition, unlike nonselective lorazepam. This is direct controlled human evidence that alpha2-preferring GABA-A activation does not produce psychomotor slowing; benzodiazepine psychomotor impairment should not be credited to alpha2.

drugs: TPA023, an alpha2/alpha3-selective GABA-A partial agonist tested in humans
other_targets_they_hit: GABRA2 - TPA023 cannot separate alpha3 from alpha2

references.quote: binds with equivalent high (subnanomolar) affinity to the benzodiazepine binding site of recombinant human GABA(A) receptors containing an alpha1, alpha2, alpha3, or alpha5 subunit but has partial agonist efficacy at the alpha2 and alpha3 subtypes and essentially antagonist efficacy at the alpha1 and alpha5 subtypes

TPA023 was clearly differentiated from the nonselective agonist lorazepam in terms of saccadic eye movement and unlike lorazepam, it did not impair either postural stability, as judged by body sway, or cognition.

claims.note: Same evidence as GABRA2: the alpha2/alpha3-selective agonist TPA023 was non-sedating and non-impairing in humans. Nonselective benzodiazepine psychomotor impairment is not attributable to alpha3.

drugs: none; alpha4-containing GABA-A receptors are benzodiazepine-insensitive and no human drug selectively activates them
claims.note: Alpha4-containing receptors do not bind classical benzodiazepine-site agonists, so no human drug tests this claim. No human study of alpha4-selective activation was found.

drugs: none in the activation direction; the only alpha5-selective compound taken into humans (alpha5IA) is an INVERSE agonist, i.e. the opposite direction

references.quote: TPA023 has weak partial agonist efficacy at the alpha2 and alpha3 subtypes whereas alpha5IA has inverse agonist efficacy at the alpha5 subtype.

claims.note: Human alpha5-selective pharmacology exists only in the inverse-agonist (negative modulator) direction, where it enhanced cognition. There is no alpha5-selective agonist human study, so the activation claim has no human support and the one human alpha5 compound points the other way.

drugs: none; alpha6-containing GABA-A receptors are benzodiazepine-insensitive and largely cerebellar granule-cell restricted
claims.note: No human drug selectively activates alpha6-containing GABA-A receptors and no human study of alpha6 activation and psychomotor slowing was found.

drugs: none; no gamma-subunit-selective GABA-A drug exists for human use
claims.note: Benzodiazepine-site drugs require a gamma subunit but discriminate among alpha, not gamma, subunits; gamma1-containing receptors are in fact poorly benzodiazepine-sensitive. No human evidence found.

drugs: benzodiazepines and Z-drugs (diazepam, lorazepam, triazolam, zolpidem) - their high-affinity site requires a gamma2 subunit, but they are not gamma2-selective

references.quote: consistent detrimental residual effects on various aspects of psychomotor and cognitive functions were observed with the therapeutic doses of the various commonly prescribed hypnotic agents used as comparators, e.g. zolpidem 10 mg up to 5 h after dose administration

TPA023 was clearly differentiated from the nonselective agonist lorazepam in terms of saccadic eye movement and unlike lorazepam, it did not impair either postural stability, as judged by body sway, or cognition.

claims.note: Gamma2 is obligatory for the action of every benzodiazepine-site drug that impairs human psychomotor function, so the human evidence is permissive of gamma2 but cannot isolate it - and the alpha-subtype dissection (TPA023 non-impairing, zolpidem impairing) shows the impairment tracks the alpha subunit, not gamma2. Retained as a rodent-derived claim rather than credited with family-level human evidence.

drugs: none; no gamma3-selective GABA-A drug exists for human use
claims.note: No human drug selectively activates gamma3-containing GABA-A receptors. No human evidence found.

drugs: lorcaserin (selective 5-HT2C agonist, phase 3 programme)
mCPP (nonselective 5-HT2C agonist used in challenge studies)
other_targets_they_hit: HTR2A and HTR2B at higher exposures; mCPP also hits 5-HT1A/1B/1D and SERT
claims.symptom_the_human_data_support: fatigue (with dizziness and headache)

references.quote: Additional adverse events occurring in >5% of patients receiving lorcaserin included dizziness, fatigue, nausea, dry mouth and constipation in patients without diabetes

claims.note: Pooled phase 3 data for the selective 5-HT2C agonist lorcaserin list fatigue, dizziness and headache among adverse events in >5% of patients, with no psychomotor retardation or motor slowing reported. The human data support fatigue, which is a different symptom from psychomotor retardation.

Patients with KCNN2 variants had motor and language developmental delay, intellectual disability often associated with early-onset movement disorders comprising cerebellar ataxia and/or extrapyramidal symptoms.

claims.note: No human SK2 activator exists. The only human KCNN2 data are LOSS-of-function variants causing a neurodevelopmental movement disorder with ataxia, extrapyramidal signs and motor developmental delay - the opposite direction to the claim, so it is reported here as contradicting rather than credited as supporting genetic evidence.

drugs: none in the activation direction; the only KCa3.1-directed human drug, senicapoc, is a BLOCKER (opposite direction)
claims.note: KCNN4/KCa3.1 is largely non-neuronal in humans and the only clinical-stage compound is an inhibitor developed for sickle cell disease. No human evidence for activation-induced psychomotor slowing was found.

drugs: spiradoline (U-62,066E)
enadoline
and other arylacetamide kappa agonists studied in humans
other_targets_they_hit: spiradoline is highly kappa-selective; dysphoria and sedation at sub-analgesic doses are attributed to central kappa agonism

references.quote: Spiradoline is highly selective for the kappa receptor with K(i) of 8.6 nM in guinea pig.
The available clinical data suggest that spiradoline produces disturbing adverse effects such as diuresis, sedation, and dysphoria at doses lower than those needed for analgesic effects.

claims.note: A clinical pharmacology review of a highly kappa-selective agonist states that in humans the dose-limiting effects are diuresis, sedation and dysphoria. Sedation and dysphoria, not psychomotor retardation, are what the human data support.

drugs: none; all sodium-channel drugs in human use (phenytoin, carbamazepine, lacosamide, lidocaine, flecainide) are BLOCKERS acting on the pore-forming alpha subunits

drugs: ecopipam (selective D1/D5 antagonist), phase 2b randomised trial in Tourette syndrome
other_targets_they_hit: DRD5 - ecopipam is a D1-family (D1/D5) antagonist and cannot separate the two
claims.symptom_the_human_data_support: fatigue and somnolence (and insomnia), not psychomotor retardation

references.quote: ecopipam, a first-in-class, selective dopamine 1 receptor antagonist, reduces tics with a low risk for these adverse events
Headache (15.8%), insomnia (14.5%), fatigue (7.9%), and somnolence (7.9%) were the most common adverse events.

claims.note: The only selective D1-family antagonist in controlled human trials produced headache, insomnia, fatigue and somnolence at ~8% each, with no psychomotor retardation, bradykinesia or extrapyramidal signs reported. The honest human label is fatigue/somnolence, and DRD5 remains unseparated.

drugs: haloperidol
chlorpromazine
olanzapine
risperidone and antipsychotics generally
other_targets_they_hit: ADRA1A/ADRA1B - most antipsychotics are multi-target; haloperidol and amisulpride/sulpiride are the closest to D2-preferring
claims.symptom_the_human_data_support: bradykinesia / drug-induced parkinsonism

references.quote: Using a statistical cut-point derived from normative data, 64% of the patients met criterion for bradykinesia compared with 46% using a conventional observer-based severity rating scale.

Recognizing drug-induced parkinsonian bradykinesia in psychosis patients can be challenging due to overlapping presentation with psychomotor slowing associated with depression, negative symptoms, or cognitive disturbances.

claims.verdict: keep but relabel to bradykinesia (drug-induced parkinsonism)
claims.note: Objective kinematic measurement in antipsychotic-treated patients found 64% met criterion for bradykinesia, and the same paper explicitly distinguishes drug-induced parkinsonian bradykinesia from the psychomotor slowing of depression or negative symptoms. D2 blockade is the shared principal action of the class, so the claim survives in human data but as bradykinesia/parkinsonism, not psychomotor retardation.

drugs: atomoxetine (selective noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor)
reboxetine
other_targets_they_hit: atomoxetine is NET-selective; at high occupancy it also raises prefrontal dopamine via NET
claims.symptom_the_human_data_support: somnolence and fatigue, not psychomotor retardation

references.quote: Adverse events reported significantly more frequently with atomoxetine were decreased appetite, somnolence, and fatigue.

claims.note: In a randomised placebo-controlled paediatric trial the adverse events significantly more frequent on the selective NET inhibitor were decreased appetite, somnolence and fatigue. NET inhibitors are arousal-promoting drugs; the human signal is somnolence/fatigue, which the task instructions say must not be equated with psychomotor retardation.

drugs: aprepitant (and fosaprepitant/rolapitant), selective NK1 receptor antagonists
other_targets_they_hit: none of consequence for the CNS effect; aprepitant is given with ondansetron and dexamethasone in the cited trials, which is a co-medication confound
claims.symptom_the_human_data_support: asthenia and fatigue

references.quote: Aprepitant (Emend) is the first commercially available drug from a new class of agents, the neurokinin NK(1) receptor antagonists.
The most common adverse events in randomised trials were asthenia or fatigue.

claims.note: The clinical pharmacology review of the first selective NK1 antagonist states the most common adverse events in randomised trials were asthenia or fatigue. No psychomotor retardation is reported for NK1 antagonists, including in the depression programmes.

drugs: scopolamine, benztropine, diphenhydramine, tricyclics and other antimuscarinics in overdose
other_targets_they_hit: CHRM5 - no M1-selective antagonist is in human use; co-ingested drugs also block H1 and monoamine transporters
claims.symptom_the_human_data_support: agitation / delirium

references.quote: The spectrum of anticholinergic delirium ranges from mild agitation to severe behavioural disturbance.

claims.note: A toxicology case series states that anticholinergic delirium ranges from mild agitation to severe behavioural disturbance, and the catatonia pharmacovigilance study independently flags benztropine. The human symptom is agitated delirium, not locomotor hyperactivity, and the drugs block all five muscarinic subtypes so M1 cannot be isolated.

esketamine
